Wilson was renominated at the [1916 Democratic National Convention](/wiki/1916_Democratic_National_Convention "1916 Democratic National Convention") without opposition.[[195]](#cite_note-196) In an effort to win progressive voters, Wilson called for legislation providing for an eight-hour day and six-day workweek, health and safety measures, the prohibition of child labor, and safeguards for female workers. He also favored a minimum wage for all work performed by and for the federal government.[[196]](#cite_note-197) The Democrats also campaigned on the slogan "He Kept Us Out of War", and warned that a Republican victory would mean war with Germany.[[197]](#cite_note-198) Hoping to reunify the progressive and conservative wings of the party, the [1916 Republican National Convention](/wiki/1916_Republican_National_Convention "1916 Republican National Convention") nominated Supreme Court justice [Charles Evans Hughes](/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes") for president; as a jurist, he had been completely out of politics by 1912. fanoutqa_038816.t: Summon the Suit :: Reception :: Viewership :: chunk_0008
fanoutqa_038816.x:
Summon the Suit :: Reception :: Viewership :: chunk_0008
According to market research company Parrot Analytics, which looks at consumer engagement in consumer research, streaming, downloads, and on social media, *Moon Knight* ranked as the sixth most in-demand digital original series for the week of April 2–8. The series achieved demand 34 times higher than the average show, reflecting a substantial 65% increase from the previous week.[[25]](#cite_note-25) [Nielsen Media Research](/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research"), which records streaming viewership on U.S. television screens, reported that it was the third-most watched original series across streaming services for the week of April 4–10 with 608 million minutes watched,[[26]](#cite_note-MinutesWatched-26) which was a 45% increase from the previous week.[[27]](#cite_note-PremiereMinutes-27) The streaming aggregator Reelgood, which monitors real-time data from 5 million users in the U.S. for original and acquired streaming programs and movies across subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) and ad-supported video-on-demand (AVOD) services, reported that it was the second most-streamed program in the U.S. for the week ending April 6.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-ReelGood-29) [JustWatch](/wiki/JustWatch "JustWatch"), a guide to streaming content with access to data from more than 20 million users around the world, estimated that *Moon Knight* was the second most-streamed series in the U.S. from April 4–10.[[30]](#cite_note-JustWatch-30) [Whip Media](/wiki/Whip_Media "Whip Media"), which tracks viewership data for the more than 21 million worldwide users of its [TV Time](/wiki/TV_Time "TV Time") app, revealed that it was the most-streamed original series for the week ending April 10.[[31]](#cite_note-TVTime-31)

fanoutqa_010912.t: Scarlett Johansson :: Acting career :: 2003–2004: Transition to adult roles :: part 01 :: chunk_0005
fanoutqa_010912.x:
Scarlett Johansson :: Acting career :: 2003–2004: Transition to adult roles :: part 01 :: chunk_0005
Johansson transitioned from teen to adult roles with two films in 2003: the romantic comedy-drama *[Lost in Translation](/wiki/Lost_in_Translation_(film) "Lost in Translation (film)")* and the drama *[Girl with a Pearl Earring](/wiki/Girl_with_a_Pearl_Earring_(film) "Girl with a Pearl Earring (film)")*.[[38]](#cite_note-UtusanAdultRoles-38) In the former, directed by [Sofia Coppola](/wiki/Sofia_Coppola "Sofia Coppola"), she played Charlotte, a listless and lonely young wife, opposite [Bill Murray](/wiki/Bill_Murray "Bill Murray"). Coppola had first noticed Johansson in *Manny & Lo*, and compared her to a young [Lauren Bacall](/wiki/Lauren_Bacall "Lauren Bacall"); Coppola based the film's story on the relationship between Bacall and [Humphrey Bogart](/wiki/Humphrey_Bogart "Humphrey Bogart") in *[The Big Sleep](/wiki/The_Big_Sleep_(1946_film) "The Big Sleep (1946 film)")* (1946).[[39]](#cite_note-39) Johansson found the experience of working with a female director different because of Coppola's ability to empathize with her.[[40]](#cite_note-40) Made on a budget of $4 million, the film grossed $119 million at the box office and received critical acclaim.[[41]](#cite_note-41)[[42]](#cite_note-42) [Roger Ebert](/wiki/Roger_Ebert "Roger Ebert") was pleased with the film and described the lead actors' performances as "wonderful",[[43]](#cite_note-43) and *[Entertainment Weekly](/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* wrote of Johansson's "embracing, restful serenity".[[44]](#cite_note-44) *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* praised Johansson, aged seventeen at the time of filming, for playing an older character.[[45]](#cite_note-45)

fanoutqa_024992.t: French Bulldog :: Health :: Life expectancy :: chunk_0007
fanoutqa_024992.x:
French Bulldog :: Health :: Life expectancy :: chunk_0007
A study of the deaths of 30,563 dogs of different breeds in the United Kingdom in 2016–2020 found the French Bulldog to have a life expectancy at birth of 4.53 years, the lowest by a large margin of all breeds in the study, which found an average for all dogs of 11.23 years.[[38]](#cite_note-sr-38): 1 This same study indicates that the low life expectancy for French Bulldogs is possibly influenced by the increasing number of French Bulldogs present in the UK, increasing from 2,771 KC registered individuals in 2011 to 39,266 individuals in 2020, skewing the general population to be very young on average and biasing the data.[[38]](#cite_note-sr-38): 1 A Japanese study of pet cemetery data found the French Bulldog to have a life expectancy of 10.2 years, the lowest of all breeds in the study.[[39]](#cite_note-39)[[a]](#cite_note-40) A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.8 years for the breed compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds and 12 for [crossbreeds](/wiki/Mongrel "Mongrel").[[40]](#cite_note-41)

French Bulldogs frequently require [Caesarean section](/wiki/Caesarean_section "Caesarean section") to give birth, with over 80% of litters delivered this way.[[41]](#cite_note-42)[[42]](#cite_note-Telegraph-CSection-43)

A UK study identified French Bulldog bitches to be 15.9 times more likely to experience dystocia.[[43]](#cite_note-44)

French Bulldogs are prone to having congenital [hemivertebrae](/wiki/Congenital_vertebral_anomaly "Congenital vertebral anomaly") (also called "[butterfly vertebrae](/wiki/Butterfly_vertebrae "Butterfly vertebrae")").[[44]](#cite_note-45)[[45]](#cite_note-46)

A review of more than 200,000 patients in the UK found that French Bulldogs had a noticeably higher occurrence of [patellar luxation](/wiki/Patellar_luxation "Patellar luxation") with the French Bulldog having an odds ratio of 5.4.[[46]](#cite_note-47)

MacLaren's, an Irish bar in the middle of New York City, in which a lot of the show is set, is loosely based on four of Bays and Thomas's favorite bars: McGee's, a Midtown tavern near the [Ed Sullivan Theater](/wiki/Ed_Sullivan_Theater "Ed Sullivan Theater") where the *Late Show* is taped; McHale's, a legendary [Hell's Kitchen](/wiki/Hell%27s_Kitchen "Hell's Kitchen") bar which closed in 2006; [Chumley's](/wiki/Chumley%27s "Chumley's"), a since-closed historic Greenwich Village pub; and Fez, another closed bar on the Upper West Side.[[15]](#cite_note-15) McGee's had a [mural](/wiki/Mural "Mural") that Bays and Thomas both liked and wanted to incorporate into the show.[[16]](#cite_note-16) The name for the bar is from Carter Bays' assistant, Carl MacLaren; the bartender in the show is also named Carl.[[17]](#cite_note-keller-17)

Episodes were generally shot over a three-day period in the [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles")-based Soundstage Studio 22[[18]](#cite_note-18) and featured upwards of 50 scenes with quick transitions and [flashbacks](/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)"). However, the [pilot episode](/wiki/Pilot_(How_I_Met_Your_Mother) "Pilot (How I Met Your Mother)") was filmed at [CBS Radford](/wiki/CBS_Radford "CBS Radford").[[19]](#cite_note-19) The [laugh track](/wiki/Laugh_track "Laugh track") was later created by recording an audience being shown the final edited episode. Thomas claimed that shooting before a live audience would have been impossible because of the structure of the show and the numerous [flashforwards](/wiki/Flashforward "Flashforward") in each episode and because doing so "would blur the line between 'audience' and 'hostage situation'".[[20]](#cite_note-ryan2-20) Later seasons started filming in front of an audience on occasion, when smaller sets were used.

During her grandfather's reign, Elizabeth was third in the [line of succession to the British throne](/wiki/Line_of_succession_to_the_British_throne "Line of succession to the British throne"), behind her uncle [Edward, Prince of Wales](/wiki/Edward_VIII "Edward VIII"), and her father. Although her birth generated public interest, she was not expected to become queen, as Edward was still young and expected to marry and have children of his own, who would precede Elizabeth in the line of succession.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBond20068Lacey200276Pimlott20013-19) When [her grandfather died](/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_George_V "Death and state funeral of George V") in 1936 and her uncle succeeded as Edward VIII, she became second in line to the throne, after her father. Later that year, [Edward abdicated](/wiki/Abdication_of_Edward_VIII "Abdication of Edward VIII"), after his proposed marriage to divorced American socialite [Wallis Simpson](/wiki/Wallis_Simpson "Wallis Simpson") provoked a [constitutional crisis](/wiki/Constitutional_crisis "Constitutional crisis").[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELacey200297–98-20) Consequently, Elizabeth's father became king, taking the [regnal name](/wiki/Regnal_name "Regnal name") George VI. Since Elizabeth had no brothers, she became [heir presumptive](/wiki/Heir_presumptive "Heir presumptive"). If her parents had subsequently had a son, he would have been [heir apparent](/wiki/Heir_apparent "Heir apparent") and before her in the line of succession, which was determined by the [male-preference primogeniture](/wiki/Male-preference_primogeniture "Male-preference primogeniture") in effect at the time.[[19]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarr201178,_85Pimlott200171–73-21)

fanoutqa_033952.t: List of tallest buildings in Hyderabad :: History :: Policy Shifts and the Vertical Boom (Late 2010s–2020s) :: chunk_0003
fanoutqa_033952.x:
List of tallest buildings in Hyderabad :: History :: Policy Shifts and the Vertical Boom (Late 2010s–2020s) :: chunk_0003
In 2014, the state of [Andhra Pradesh](/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh "Andhra Pradesh") was bifurcated into two states – [Telangana](/wiki/Telangana "Telangana") and Andhra Pradesh, with Hyderabad being geographically located in Telangana. The newly formed [Government of Telangana](/wiki/Government_of_Telangana "Government of Telangana") relaxed [floor space index (FSI)](/wiki/Floor_area_ratio "Floor area ratio") norms and provided faster approvals for new projects with the goal of spurring growth in the [newly formed state](/wiki/Telangana_movement "Telangana movement"). Developmental reforms such as the [Telangana Building Permission Approval and Self-Certification System](/wiki/TS-iPASS "TS-iPASS") (TS-bPASS)[[10]](#cite_note-:29-10) coupled with an influx of real estate investments led to the announcement of several new high-rise projects. Between the late 2010s and early 2020s, Hyderabad witnessed a rapid construction boom, particularly around its IT corridor in the west. This was fuelled by an increase of [foreign investment](/wiki/Foreign_direct_investment_in_India "Foreign direct investment in India") from global technology firms and a rapidly growing [upper-middle-class](/wiki/Upper_middle_class "Upper middle class") population.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

In the early 2020s, major developers like My Home Group, SAS Infra, Auro Realty, and RMZ launched large-scale residential and commercial skyscrapers in areas such as [HITEC City](/wiki/HITEC_City "HITEC City"), [Kokapet](/wiki/Kokapet "Kokapet"), [Nanakramguda](/wiki/Nanakramguda "Nanakramguda"), and [Puppalaguda](/wiki/Puppalguda "Puppalguda"). The completion of SAS Crown in 2025 marked Hyderabad's entry into the 200m+ skyscraper league.[[4]](#cite_note-:4-4) [Residential high-rise](/wiki/Tower_block "Tower block") gated communities with 40–50 floors became increasingly popular.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

Texas A&M is part of the Texas A&M University System, which consists of eleven universities, eight state agencies, and the RELLIS Campus. The system is governed by a ten-member [Board of Regents](/wiki/Texas_A%26M_University_System#Governance_and_administration "Texas A&M University System"), nine of whom are appointed by the Governor of Texas to six-year terms, and one non-voting Student Regent who is appointed to a one-year term. The Chancellor of the Texas A&M University System is responsible for day-to-day operations and is answerable to the Board of Regents.[[94]](#cite_note-AdminStructure-97)[[95]](#cite_note-OrgChart-98)[[96]](#cite_note-99)

The university is led by the university president, who has executive responsibility, and is selected by and reports to the chancellor. The provost is responsible for all educational and service activities of the university, and reports to the president. The cabinet, as the institution's administrative arm, and the deans of the respective colleges, also report to the president.[[94]](#cite_note-AdminStructure-97)[[95]](#cite_note-OrgChart-98) The university and colleges are accredited by the [Southern Association of Colleges and Schools](/wiki/Southern_Association_of_Colleges_and_Schools "Southern Association of Colleges and Schools") and associated professional organizations offering degrees in 130 courses of study, over 260 professional and graduate degrees via its 17 colleges, and further opportunities in 21 research centers and institutes.[[97]](#cite_note-100)[[98]](#cite_note-101)[[99]](#cite_note-102)

On the 30th anniversary of the *Forbes* list of the world's billionaires, for the fourth year in a row, [Bill Gates](/wiki/Bill_Gates "Bill Gates") was named the richest man in the world.[[5]](#cite_note-Forbes-2017-5) In 2017, there was a record of 2,043 people on the list, which is the first time over 2,000 people were listed. This included 195 newcomers of whom 76 were from China and 25 from the U.S.; there were 56 people under 40 and it had a record of 227 women.[[20]](#cite_note-20) The number of billionaires increased 13% to 2,043 from 1,810 in 2016; this was the biggest change in over 30 years of tracking billionaires globally.[[5]](#cite_note-Forbes-2017-5) Added together, the total net worth for 2017's billionaires was US$7.67 trillion, up from US$7.1 trillion in 2015.[[5]](#cite_note-Forbes-2017-5)[[21]](#cite_note-Forbes-list-2015-21) This was the first time after 12 years that [Carlos Slim](/wiki/Carlos_Slim "Carlos Slim") was not within the top five. The U.S. had the most billionaires in the world, with a record of 565. China had 319 (not including Hong Kong, Taiwan or Macau), Germany had 114, and India had the fourth most with 101; India reached over 100 billionaires for its first time.

Western Front (World War II) :: 1939–1940: Axis victories :: Phoney War :: chunk_0004
Main article: [Phoney War](/wiki/Phoney_War "Phoney War")

The Phoney War was an early phase of World War II marked by a few military operations in [Continental Europe](/wiki/Continental_Europe "Continental Europe") in the months following the German invasion of Poland and preceding the [Battle of France](/wiki/Battle_of_France "Battle of France"). Although the great [powers](/wiki/Power_(international) "Power (international)") of Europe had [declared war](/wiki/Declaration_of_war "Declaration of war") on one another, neither side had yet committed to launching a significant attack, and there was relatively little fighting on the ground. This was also the period in which the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") and France did not supply significant aid to Poland, despite their [pledged alliance](/wiki/Anglo-Polish_alliance "Anglo-Polish alliance").

The French forces launched a small offensive, the [Saar Offensive](/wiki/Saar_Offensive "Saar Offensive") against Germany in the [Saar region](/wiki/Saarland "Saarland") but halted their advance and returned. While most of the German Army was fighting against Poland, a much smaller German force manned the [Siegfried Line](/wiki/Siegfried_Line "Siegfried Line"), their fortified defensive line along the French border. At the [Maginot Line](/wiki/Maginot_Line "Maginot Line") on the other side of the border, French troops stood facing them, whilst the [British Expeditionary Force](/wiki/British_Expeditionary_Force_(World_War_II) "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)") and other elements of the [French Army](/wiki/French_Army "French Army") created a defensive line along the Belgian border. There were only some local, minor skirmishes.
